macros.name: backlevel
macros.doc: Levels can be arbitrarily traversed with commands \steplevel and \backlevel.

macros.name: diagrambottom
macros.doc: To set the top or bottom of all future (non-analysis) diagrams at once, the commands \diagramtop and \diagrambottom can be redefined with \renewcommand.

macros.name: DiagramCache
macros.doc: By default, the number of diagrams that can be held in memory is 3. It can be enlarged with the command \DiagramCache{⟨number⟩}.

macros.name: diagramtop
macros.doc: To set the top or bottom of all future (non-analysis) diagrams at once, the commands \diagramtop and \diagrambottom can be redefined with \renewcommand.

macros.name: makediagrams
macros.doc: The diagrams are actually typeset with the command \makediagrams. This command will typeset, in principle, all diagrams in memory, framed and separated by \hfill’s.

macros.name: makediagrams
macros.doc: The diagrams are actually typeset with the command \makediagrams. This command will typeset, in principle, all diagrams in memory, framed and separated by \hfill’s.

macros.name: makediagramsfont
macros.doc: All the text typeset by \makediagrams is subject to \makediagramsfont. By default it means \small, but it can be changed at any point.

macros.name: position
macros.doc: \position is designed for quick diagram drawing (where it does not matter who can castle where, etc.).

macros.name: position
macros.doc: \position is designed for quick diagram drawing (where it does not matter who can castle where, etc.).

macros.name: preparediagram
macros.doc: sends the current position into diagram cache, not with the usual header and footer (which by default are the players’ names and the last move, as explained in section 3.5), but with those set directly by the user.

macros.name: resigns
macros.doc: \resigns issues \whitewins if it’s \drawn Black’s turn, or \blackwins if it’s White’s.

macros.name: SkakOff
macros.doc: If, for any reason, the capabilities of skak are an obstacle rather than a utility, skak can be turned off with \SkakOff.

macros.name: steplevel
macros.doc: Levels can be arbitrarily traversed with commands \steplevel and \backlevel.

macros.name: takes
macros.doc: Predefined essentially as $\times$, you can \renewcommand\takes to substitute your favorite sign for captures (a colon? nothing?).

macros.name: TheDiagram
macros.doc: The number is formatted by the current version of \TheDiagram—by default something like ‘4 ’.

macros.name: threat
macros.doc: Simple threats with the command \threat<⟨threat⟩>. TEXmate inserts the symbol E and typesets the ⟨threat⟩ without regard to move numbers, etc.

macros.name: Threat
macros.doc: With \Threat<hthreatened variationi>, TEXmate will typeset the hthreatened variationi with appropriate move numbers, etc. Unlike \threat, \Threat does not include the E sign, but this can be added to the first move if necessary.

macros.name: toD
macros.doc: \toD has an argument: the last move. TEXmate will typeset the last move and put it (by default) below the diagram.

macros.name: toD*
macros.doc: \toD has an argument: the last move. TEXmate will typeset the last move and put it (by default) below the diagram.

macros.name: varfont
macros.doc: \varfont, which is originally equivalent to \bfseries, but can be changed.
